messages:
mike: @channel P1 alert — we're seeing a routing storm. Several Dedicated tenants (prod-*) are being sent to the hosted pool, causing elevated latencies and 503s. Impacting multiple customers. Observability: backend error rate +15% and latency +300ms. paging oncall now :rotating_light:
incident-bot: PAGED oncall@sre — P1: routing-fallback spike for capacity-tier DEDICATED -> HOSTED. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/routing-fallback

sara: acked. joining call in 2. grabbing bridge. tagging infra & platform.
raj: on it. initial look — I think this started right after rollout of the new fallback policy at 03:14 UTC. Policy precedence seems inverted for capacity-tier mapping, so when dedicated pool is busy we incorrectly pick hosted variant even when tenant isolation should prevent it.
emily: customers reporting degraded completions and occasional hallucinations due to model variant mismatch (hosted uses quantized v2, dedicated uses v3-8b). want quick mitigation first, then rollback.

alice: creating temp rule to force strict isolation for affected tenant group (prod-*) until we fix policy logic. applying via admin CLI now.
ops-bot: ACTION: set-routes --scope tenants:prod-* --set routing.strict_isolation=true --expires 15m — initiated by alice

mike: good. that should stop spillover. once applied, verify that the routing graph shows tenants pinned to dedicated pools and error rate drops.

raj: confirmed — applied config. here's the command I ran:
```
redwood-admin routing update --selector "tenant:prod-*" \
  --set "fallback.policy=none" \
  --set "routing.strict_isolation=true" \
  --reason "emergency mitigation: P1 routing spillover"
```

raj: metrics already improving. 503s down ~70% in the last 30s, p95 latency trending down.
sara: great — keep monitor. open a rollback PR for the policy change in the feature branch. we'll revert the rollout and run unit + integration tests before re-release.

emily: starting customer-impact note. affected customers list so far: [acme-corp, brightmaps, credo-ai]. severity: degraded (timeouts/partial results), SLAs at risk. contacting account leads.

mike: who deployed the policy? need commit id and reviewer.
raj: it was rolled by infra-deploy bot as part of canary rollout: commit 3a7b9f2 -> rollout id r-2026-03-15-03. I see the policy json had an accidental precedence field set to "LOWER" instead of "HIGHER" for dedicated-binding. that flips selection when both matches exist.
alice: opening hotfix PR to correct precedence and add a unit test that simulates capacity exhaustion -> ensure dedicated wins when tenant has isolation tag.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE — mitigation applied: temporary strict isolation set, rollback PR opened (PR #4021), oncall: sara, lead: raj, status: mitigated -> monitoring.

mike: plan for next 30m: 1) keep temporary isolation for 15-60m while we validate, 2) merge hotfix PR after tests, 3) roll back the canary rollout (r-2026-03-15-03) and re-deploy corrected policy, 4) postmortem and customer comms draft.

sara: I've informed support to hold off on broad comms until we confirm full recovery. Emily, please prepare a short message for affected accounts.
emily: will do. draft: "We're investigating an internal routing change that temporarily routed some traffic to an incompatible hosted model variant causing degraded responses. We've applied an emergency fix and are rolling back the change. We'll follow up with details and remediation steps."

raj: to add technical notes for postmortem — failure mode: precedence inversion in policy evaluator + missing regression for capacity-tier semantics. replication steps captured in the hotfix PR.

alice: also increased dedicated pool autoscaler thresholds as a short-term relief so we don't hit the fallback as easily. changed min_replicas from 2 -> 4 for affected pool.

mike: heads-up: customers on Dedicated should not have been allowed to fall back to hosted by design. this is a high-priority SLA violation. flagging billing & legal for risk assessment.

ops-bot: RUNBOOK CHECK: all required mitigation steps completed? [applied_isolation, rollback_pr, increased_capacity, account_notifications] -> yes/partial/partial/queued

sara: monitoring window. if we see recurrence after we remove the temp isolation, we'll escalate to oncall-4 and trigger full incident bridge.

raj: patch merged to main in hotfix PR #4021. CI green. I'm scheduling a controlled rollback of the canary now (will pause rollout traffic).

ops-bot: ROLLBACK: rollback rollout r-2026-03-15-03 -> initiated by raj. expected completion ~2m.

mike: verify post-rollback that policy precedence is correct in policy graph and run a traffic replay test for affected tenants.

raj: rollback complete. policy graph shows precedence=HIGHER for dedicated-binding. running replay against staging harness.
emily: customer impact doc updated and sent to account leads for the three affected customers. asking if anyone saw data loss — none reported, only degraded/incorrect responses.

alice: removing temporary strict_isolation flag now (expires still set but I'm clearing it to let corrected policy take effect).

raj: final checks — 503 count back to baseline, latency back to normal for prod tenants. no new errors after 6m.
sara: closing incident in 10m if stable. schedule postmortem for tomorrow 15:00 UTC and assign owners: raj (root cause), alice (mitigation timeline), emily (customer comms), mike (action items + follow-up).

mike: thanks everyone. reminder to update the runbook with the new guardrail test for policy precedence and add an integration test to the e2e suite.

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED — status: recovered, severity downgraded to P3 for follow-up. Postmortem task created: TASK-7893.

sara: closing notes: primary cause = policy precedence bug in fallback rollout; mitigation = emergency strict isolation + rollback + autoscaler bump; follow-ups = tests, runbook updates, customer follow-ups. good coordination. :thumbsup:

mike: filing a short post-incident blameless summary for execs. will attach timeline and metrics.

alice: creating retrospective doc now and will link to TASK-7893.

emily: will send comms update to account leads in 30m and a more detailed email after the postmortem.

mike: thread closed after postmortem scheduled. thank you all for quick response.
